primitives.name: Storybook Fidelity Oracle
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Storybook source shape Storybook is the **fidelity oracle, not the runtime**.
primitives.assumptions: Runtime fidelity requires browser execution of story modules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When story code diverges from runtime artifact, visual mismatch occurs.

primitives.name: Side-by-Side Compare Harness
primitives.verbatim_quote: The repo's own storybook render is the ground truth those previews must match: a compare harness screenshots each story in the reference storybook and the matching preview render side by side, and you iterate until they match.
primitives.assumptions: Visual alignment ensures functional equivalence of story implementations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mismatched renders indicate divergent story logic or rendering paths.

layer2.mapping: Harness enables iterative refinement through visual feedback loops.
layer2.telemetry: Pixel-level difference metrics between reference and preview iframe.html.

primitives.name: Browser-Based Runtime Execution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Nothing from storybook-static is uploaded, and no story code is ever evaluated at build time - stories run only in the browser, against the real artifact.
primitives.assumptions: Build-time abstraction cannot replicate interactive runtime behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Static builds fail to capture dynamic component interactions.

layer2.mapping: Runtime execution validates story fidelity against actual artifact behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Execution trace consistency between storybook and preview environments.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that Storybook acts as a fidelity oracle by enforcing runtime equivalence through browser-based story evaluation. This creates a dualism: the static build process must produce artifacts that behave identically when executed in the browser versus during development. The compare harness serves as a verification kernel, iterating until pixel-perfect alignment between reference and preview renders. The system assumes that any deviation from this alignment indicates either incorrect story implementation or environmental inconsistency. Failure modes include misaligned imports, missing dependencies in bundled artifacts, or incorrect resolution of component paths. The runtime execution primitive ensures that all story logic is evaluated within the same environment as end-users, preventing false positives from static analysis. The derived kernel of the compare harness enables continuous refinement through visual feedback, forming a closed-loop validation system.
